key_insight: MUSE captured scale- and direction-dependent glioma MRI heterogeneity, with substantial overlap with directional radiomics rather than clearly independent molecular information.
clinical_relevance: These imaging measurements may support research into glioma characterization, but the study does not establish clinical utility or evaluate cancer drug discovery.
method: Analyzed postcontrast T1-weighted MRI and enhancing-tumor segmentations from UCSF-PDGM.
Compared native 3D MUSE variograms with directional GLCM radiomics and tested associations with IDH status.
Evaluated a separate 3D residual CNN for image-based IDH classification.
evidence_signal: Among 416 patients, including 375 with paired radiomics, aligned MUSE and GLCM measurements correlated strongly (r = 0.954); the independent CNN achieved out-of-fold IDH ROC-AUC 0.792.
watch_item: In the grade-4 subgroup, only 24 of 364 tumors were IDH-mutant, and the MUSE–IDH association was attenuated after directional GLCM adjustment (p = 0.256).
paper_title: Multiscale Spatial Characterization of Glioma MRI with MUSE and Radiomics
